reasoning: The finding claims DuckDB's C API scalar-function wrapper passes constant-vector arguments (e.g. the SQL literals 37.7749/-122.4194 in hv_jit(lat, lon, 37.7749, -122.4194)) through to the user callback un-flattened, causing haversine.py's carray reads of a_lat2[i]/a_lon2[i] for i in range(n) (lines 101-102, 107-112) to read out of bounds past a 1-element constant buffer. This is refuted by DuckDB's own source: src/main/capi/scalar_function-c.cpp's CAPIScalarFunction (the function actually registered as ScalarFunction::function and invoked by the expression evaluator on every call) executes `auto all_const = input.AllConstant(); input.Flatten();` UNCONDITIONALLY before reinterpret_casting the chunk and invoking the user's duckdb_scalar_function_t callback. DataChunk::Flatten() materializes every vector, including ones that started as CONSTANT_VECTOR from a BoundConstantExpression, into a FLAT_VECTOR with the value broadcast to all n rows -- so by the time the callback runs, lat2/lon2 are already flat n-element arrays. The subsequent `if (all_const && ...) result.SetVectorType(CONSTANT_VECTOR)` only re-collapses the OUTPUT vector for optimization; it does not affect what the callback reads. I verified this Flatten() call is present, in the identical form, in the duckdb/duckdb source at both v1.3.2 and v1.5.1 (the endpoints of numbduck's pin duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6), fetched via `gh api repos/duckdb/duckdb/contents/src/main/capi/scalar_function-c.cpp?ref=<tag>`. So the premise 'DuckDB does not flatten scalar-function argument vectors before invoking the C-API callback' is factually false for the entire supported version range, there is no out-of-bounds read, and haversine.py's kernel (examples/haversine.py:88-113) is correct as written. Severity corrected to none (finding does not survive verification).
